reporting-org.narrative: The Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria

title.narrative: To ensure provision of quality care and prevention services for all people in Kenya with TB, leprosy and lung diseases

description.narrative: Kenya - Tuberculosis - The National Treasury & Economic Planning of the Government of Kenya - TNT. This program has the following goals: Contribute to attainment of universal health coverage through comprehensive TB/HIV prevention, treatment and care for all people in kenya.. To ensure provision of quality care and prevention services for all people in Kenya with Tuberculosis.. To provide all Kenyans with 100% coverage on essential health services. The objectives of this program are: Reduce the TB incidence rate by 80% by 2030 compared to 2015. To build sustainable resilient systems for health and community, preparedness for emergency, pandemic, and response to in-country public health events to limit transmission, morbidity, and mortality by strengthening integrated disease surveillance and deployment of community-based surveillance systems.. Reduce TB deaths by 90% compared by 2030 compared to 2015. To build a motivated, skilled, equitably distributed health and community workforce through capacity building, supportive supervision and deployment of digital tools and integrated health information system.. Strengthening the timely generation and use of integrated, comprehensive and good-quality health information. To improve the supply of quality medical oxygen through the procurement of bulk oxygen sources, oxygen distribution infrastructure and improved access of respiratory care and therapeutics. To strengthen laboratory systems at national and subnational levels for early detection and monitoring of disease outbreaks, identifying emerging pathogens, and informing public health decision-making by development and dissemination of guidelines, expanding integrated simple referral and multi-disease testing platforms.. Increasing access to care that is equitable in terms of quality and availability of services at all levels, including emergency care

Number of health facilities participating in HAI/AMR surveillance

Percentage of laboratories showing adequate performance in external quality assurance for smear microscopy among the total number of laboratories that undertake smear microscopy during the reporting period

Percentage of HIV-positive registered TB patients given anti-retroviral therapy during TB treatment
Percentage of laboratories accredited according to ISO15189 standard or achieving at least four stars towards accreditation or two-star incremental improvement
Completeness of reporting: Percentage of expected monthly reports (for the reporting period) that are actually received
LMIS Reporting Rate - Percentage of all health facilities that are required to report that submit an LMIS report to central authority
Percentage of bacteriologically confirmed TB cases successfully treated (cured plus completed treatment) among the bacteriologically confirmed TB cases registered during a specified period
Percentage of registered new and relapse TB patients with documented HIV status
Number of TB cases (all forms) notified among prisoners
Number of notified cases of bacteriologically confirmed TB, new and relapses
Percentage of districts reporting events (per national guidelines)

Number of children <5 in contact with TB patients who began isonizide preventive therapy

Number of people with confirmed RR-TB and/or MDR-TB notified
Number of notified cases of all forms of TB (i.e. bacteriologically confirmed + clinically diagnosed), new and relapse cases
Percentage of public financial management system components used for grant financial management
Percentage of previously treated TB patients receiving DST (bacteriologically positive cases only)

Number of people in contact with TB patients who began preventive therapy

Number of notified TB cases (all forms) contributed by non-national TB program providers – community referrals
